statement: enforcer-validator's Validator trait deliberately takes ValidationInput{file:&RelPath,source:&str,scope:ScanScope} rather than walking the filesystem itself — RR-6.1 (no-naked-domain-strings) still flags the harness's own fixture-loading functions (run_fixture_parity, read_fixture, fixture_rel_path) because they take raw &str/PathBuf before branding to RelPath. This is a genuine boundary use (parse-at-boundary pattern from enforcer-domain), not a defect, but the crate is not yet in whatever allowlist/boundary-module config suppresses RR-6.1 for parse-boundary code.
why: Next validator-family crate (arc-06..13,19) authors will hit the same RR-6.1 false-positive-by-design pattern when they add their own fixture-loading glue; worth fixing the allowlist once rather than every lane rediscovering it.
howToApply: When wiring RR-6.1's boundary/owner-module allowlist (or its config surface), add enforcer-validator::harness (and likely each enforcer-lang-*::harness-adjacent module) as an owner module for String/&str/PathBuf in signatures, OR scope the rule to only domain/business-logic modules and exclude test-fixture-IO modules by convention.

evidence.ref: ocentra_enforcer_check no-naked-domain-strings on crates/enforcer-validator/src/harness.rs: 4 findings, lines 29/81/95/184, all in fixture-IO functions

statement: clippy::map_err_ignore (workspace deny lint) rejects map_err(|_| ...) even when the closure legitimately discards a lower-level error to build a higher-level one — it demands the original error be threaded through as a #[source] or io::Error::new(kind, original_error) rather than dropped. Fixed in enforcer-validator::harness::fixture_rel_path by naming and wrapping the DecodeError instead of using |_|.
why: Every crate in this workspace inherits workspace.lints.clippy with map_err_ignore=deny; a wildcard map_err on ANY Result-returning parse/decode call will fail clippy CI, not just tests.
howToApply: When converting a lower error to a crate-local error variant, name the closure parameter and pass it through (as #[source] on thiserror variants, or via io::Error::new(kind, lower_error)) instead of |_| ... — never use the wildcard pattern to discard an error value.

evidence.ref: cargo clippy -p enforcer-validator --all-targets -- -D warnings; error: map_err_ignore at harness.rs:96 before fix
